identity.name: Blue Horde
alt_names: Right wing of the Jochid ulus

land.text: the western two-fifths of the Golden Horde's 1352 shape: Crimea, the North Caucasus, the Lower Volga and the Pontic steppe

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Golden Horde row ends in 1362; the Blue and White shapes of 1363 cover 87 % of it (15,406 of 17,654 cells), the rest being the Dnieper-Dniester lands lost at Blue Waters.

land.text: the Blue Horde's lands, reunited with the White Horde by Tokhtamysh

successors.note: Cliopatria's Golden Horde row restarts in 1385; the golden-horde dossier adds golden-horde_1381 for 1381-1384.

capitals.name: Solkhat (Staryi Krym)
capitals.note: 'Mamai's old headquarters at Solkhat' in the Crimea (Mamai page). Sarai changed hands among Mamai's and Urus's khans (see the ledger) and is not given as Mamai's own seat. Coordinates are those of Staryi Krym; Solkhat is not in the gazetteer.

keyframe_review.note: 1.83 M km2 for 1363-1374 (6,936 cells): the North Caucasus, the Lower Volga and Kalmyk steppe, the Pontic steppe and most of the Crimea, from the Dnieper (31.8 E) to the Ural (60.6 E). The page has no infobox, so there is no area to compare. It says only that the Blue Horde 'stretched from the Ural River' to 'the mouths of the Danube and the Carpathians' (undated), gives three incompatible locations for the Blue Horde (east of the Volga in the Russian chronicles; the western part of the Jochid ulus in Natanzi; a Shiban appanage in western Kazakhstan) and warns of 'contradictory uses of the color terminology'. Cliopatria follows the western reading, which is Mamai's: the Mamai page puts his headquarters 'in the Crimea, centered on Solkhat'. The west edge of the shape follows the Battle of Blue Waters losses of 1362 (Kiev and Podolia to Lithuania, Moldavia independent; Blue Waters page); the Sarai and Lower Volga cities, which both Mamai's and Urus's khans held in turn, are inside the shape.

Same shape as 1363 (1.83 M km2) for 1375-1401 in Cliopatria, but the Blue Horde ends in 1380: the page says Tokhtamysh 'united the Blue Horde with the White Horde and created the Golden Horde in 1380', the Mamai page has Mamai killed at the end of 1380 or the beginning of 1381. From 1381 the shape duplicates the Golden Horde (6,858 of its 6,934 cells lie inside the Golden Horde shape of 1385, the 1385-1401 overlap of 6,581 cells named in the brief); the golden-horde dossier carries these years as its new keyframe golden-horde_1381 and its 1385 shape. Years cut to 1375-1380, shape unchanged. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1375..1380 from this entry's own 'valid for 1375-1380 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: the 1375 shape unchanged, valid for 1375-1380 only; from 1381 the land is the Golden Horde's

keyframe_review.note: 18,873 km2 (73 cells) for 1402-1439: the Crimean peninsula and nothing else (the shape lies wholly inside the gazetteer's 'Crimea' region). It is not the Blue Horde, which merged into the Golden Horde in 1380. The Edigu page has the Crimea within the Golden Horde's sphere until 'by 1412-1413, Edigu had lost control of Astrakhan, Bolghar, Crimea, and Sarai', then in the hands of Tokhtamysh's son Qadir Berdi (1419). The golden-horde dossier takes the peninsula back as a union correction on its 1385-1440 shapes, and the Crimean Khanate row starts in 1450.

correction.text: the shape unchanged but not the Blue Horde: the Crimean peninsula, to be drawn with the Golden Horde (golden-horde dossier) until 1449

keyframe_review.note: Same 18,873 km2 Crimean shape for 1440-1449 (53 vertices, identical to 1402). See blue-horde_1402. The Great Horde page, opened for the golden-horde dossier, has Crimea breaking from Sarai in August 1449; Cliopatria's Crimean Khanate starts in 1450.

correction.text: the shape unchanged but not the Blue Horde: the Crimean peninsula, Golden Horde until August 1449, then the Crimean Khanate

ledger.note: 1363: the western horde of Mamai is drawn as a state. The pages give no foundation date for a separate Blue Horde: Mamai 'proclaimed his own khan, Abdallah, in the Crimea in 1361' and Abdallah was installed at Sarai and ejected within 1362 by Murad (1362-1363); the White Horde page dates the Blue Horde's 'period of anarchy' to 1359-1380. 1363 is Cliopatria's first year (the Golden Horde row ends in 1362 after the Blue Waters defeat).

region.text: the western wing of the Jochid ulus: Crimea, the North Caucasus, the Lower Volga and Pontic steppe, Mamai's lands

ledger.note: 1373: Urus Khan of the eastern horde takes Sarai from Mamai's khan. '1373: Urus Khan ejected Muhammad-Sultan' (Mamai's puppet at Sarai); in 1374 Il Beg seized Sarai, Mamai restored Muhammad-Sultan and Urus expelled him again; 1375 Qaghan Beg took Sarai. The White Horde page dates Urus's claim to both hordes to 1375.

region.text: Sarai and the Lower Volga, the seat that changed hands between Mamai's and Urus's khans

ledger.note: Early 1380: Tokhtamysh ends the contest. 'Qaghan Beg and Arab Shah submitted to him' (1380); the Mamai page has Arab Shah yield Sarai to Tokhtamysh in early 1380.

region.text: Sarai and the Lower Volga, the seat that changed hands between Mamai's and Urus's khans

ledger.note: 1380: the Blue Horde is joined to the White Horde under Tokhtamysh. 'He united the Blue Horde with the White Horde and created the Golden Horde in 1380'; the Golden Horde infobox gives 1379.

1380: Mamai's horde ends. Mamai lost to Tokhtamysh at the Kalka and 'the agents of Tokhtamysh caught up with Mamai outside Solkhat and killed him' at the end of 1380 or the beginning of 1381 (Mamai page; the Tokhtamysh page dates the Kalka defeat to autumn 1381). The last year of the shape is 1380; the Golden Horde is drawn whole from 1381.

region.text: the Blue Horde's lands, passing to the Golden Horde

wars.name: Great Troubles
wars.outcome: Succession war after Berdi Beg's death in August 1359: Mamai makes and unmakes khans (Abdallah, Muhammad-Sultan, Tulak) while Urus Khan and then Tokhtamysh hold the eastern ulus; Tokhtamysh takes Sarai in early 1380.
wars.note: Dates as the Mamai page gives them. Reviewer ia-02-b clipped the war to this dossier's life (1363-1380): from 1359 to 1363; the pages' fuller span is in the outcome.

wars.name: Mamai's wars with Moscow (Vozha and Kulikovo)
wars.outcome: Mamai raids Nizhny Novgorod's lands and sacks Novosil in 1375 and burns Nizhny Novgorod in 1377; his army is beaten on the Vozha on 11 August 1378 and on Kulikovo Field on 8 September 1380. No land changes hands; Moscow had 'refused to pay his heavy tribute in silver'.
wars.note: Tokhtamysh restored the tribute after sacking Moscow in 1382 (Tokhtamysh page).

wars.name: Tokhtamysh's war on Mamai
wars.outcome: Mamai, beaten on the Kalka, is refused entry at Solkhat and Caffa and killed outside Solkhat; his lands pass to Tokhtamysh.
wars.note: The Mamai page puts the Kalka fight at the end of 1380 or the beginning of 1381, the Tokhtamysh page in autumn 1381. Reviewer ia-02-b clipped the war to this dossier's life (1363-1380): to 1381 to 1380; the pages' fuller span is in the outcome.

certainty.note: Steppe frontiers drawn approximate; the western edge follows the Dnieper as Lithuania left it after Blue Waters; the Sarai and Lower Volga seat was contested between the hordes.

notes:
What the Blue Horde is. The Blue Horde page admits three incompatible usages (east of the Volga; the western part of the Jochid ulus; a Shiban appanage in western Kazakhstan); Cliopatria draws the western one, which fits the Mamai page (the Crimea, Solkhat). Cliopatria's row is 1363-1449; this dossier ends it in 1380 because the Blue Horde page has Tokhtamysh unite it with the White Horde 'in 1380' (infobox of the Golden Horde: 1379; Mamai killed at the end of 1380 or the beginning of 1381). Years 1381-1401 of the 1375 shape duplicate the Golden Horde (the overlap of 6,581 cells named in the brief), and the 1402 and 1440 shapes are the Crimean peninsula, not a Blue Horde: both verdicts above, with the Crimea returned to the golden-horde dossier. The Crimea remained a Jochid dependency; it has no state of its own until the Crimean Khanate (Cliopatria 1450; the Great Horde page, opened for the golden-horde dossier, has it leave Sarai's authority in August 1449).

The start. 1363 is Cliopatria's; the pages do not date a split. The Golden Horde row (1352-1362) already contains these lands; the golden-horde dossier carries the 'split' event.

Disagreements: the Blue Waters date (1362 on the Mamai page, 'autumn 1362 or 1363' on its own page); Urus's first seizure of Sarai (1373 on the Mamai page) against 'in 1375 Urus Khan became a contested khan of both' on the White Horde page (the white-horde dossier's contest_start is 1375); the Kalka (autumn 1381 on the Tokhtamysh page).

Not written: the pre-1363 western ulus (inside the Golden Horde), Mamai's puppet khans (not a ruler list the page supports), the Genoese Crimean colonies (republic-of-genoa dossier). Gazetteer names: Solkhat / Staryi Krym (place, Crimea). Page budget: five of five.
